en.html:
Muramasa urged me to consider every tactic, including Owari no Nagare—the railgun.

For this crimson sword-armor, such advice must have been humiliating.

To expend our full strength against an unarmored human!

But humiliation had nothing to do with my refusal.

—I would kill no one again.

I had promised Ichijou: to keep asleep the curse that killed even good and innocent people.

If I used every ability of the sword-armor, I would inevitably kill him. Sword-armor was, after all, a weapon specialized for killing.

I had to restrain myself. On the oath I had sworn when I chose to follow Ichijou.

en.html:
The swordsman spoke words that could only be provocation in a mild tone that sounded nothing like provocation. Black machinery concealed his eyes, and his true intent along with them.

Yet the problem he had placed before me was precisely the reality I now faced, without exaggeration.

The enemy was alone. I too was alone. But the enemy would soon receive decisive reinforcements, while I would not...

His sword had attained the innermost mystery of Yagyuu Shinkage-ryuu, the great school crowned above all others in the martial history of this country.

Though both were called swords, it carried a different weight from the blade of Kageaki Minato, who had barely mastered an unnamed school.

Warrior and unarmored body—the difference in fighting strength that should have been absolute—might as well not exist.

—What was I to do?

By what method could I break this situation open?
